perspective:
From Arthur Chung’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, collaborating with Teresa Ortega on a community service project.
- He observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed, feels concerned, believes she needs help, and decides to offer assistance.
- He asks Teresa if he can help. He hears her say she thinks she can manage but there is a lot to do. He tells her she should take care of herself and offers to help so tasks go faster. He hears her accept help with organizing medical supplies, and they start.
- He believes Teresa’s hesitation comes from wanting to prove her capability. He feels empathy and wants to reassure her. He tells her accepting help does not mean she is incapable. He hears her say she appreciates it but wants to show she can do it herself. He responds that teamwork can be more effective and is not about proving anything. He hears her agree and say she needs reminders. He says they are in this together.
- He believes Teresa is still struggling. He feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results and wants another way to support her without making her feel inadequate. He tells her she is doing a great job. He hears her say it has been busy and she feels behind. He suggests working together and sharing the load. He hears her agree, and he says they will tackle it as a team.
- He feels hopeful that working together will ease her burden and improve efficiency, and he commits to the collaborative approach. He tells her this. He hears her say it already feels less overwhelming. He proposes handling inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins. He hears her agree and say she is glad they are working together.
- He believes their teamwork has strengthened their professional relationship, feels satisfied, and intends to maintain collaboration in future projects. He tells Teresa they accomplished more together. He hears her agree it was a great experience. He asks about continuing collaboration. He hears her call it a fantastic idea and say they have proven to be efficient and effective as a team. He says he looks forward to their next project. He hears her thank him for being supportive.

Arthur does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what she stated or what he inferred from her behavior.
